title: AWS CWI Exam Prep in Billings, MT: 6-Day Course
description: Six-day AWS CWI exam prep for Billings and Laurel refinery, pipeline, rail and fabrication inspectors: Part C code choice, Part B in Denver, eligibility.
h1: AWS CWI Exam Preparation in Billings: Six Days for Refinery, Pipeline, Rail and Fabrication Inspectors in the Yellowstone Valley
html:
Few cities of Billings' size have so much welded pressure equipment within a short drive. Two refineries sit on the edge of the city and a third operates in Laurel, a short drive west, and all three run turnarounds and maintenance programs that bring in pipefitters, welders and inspectors. Crude and refined product pipelines start and end here, BNSF trains cross the valley, and the city serves as the commercial center for a wide region of energy, agriculture and mining. Welding inspection is a steady trade in the Yellowstone Valley, and the AWS Certified Welding Inspector (CWI) credential is the common currency of that trade.

Atlantis NDT prepares Billings-area candidates for the CWI exam with a six-day course aimed at refinery and contractor welders, pipeline hands, fabrication shop quality staff, NDT technicians and engineers. The American Welding Society owns the examination: it administers each part and grants the certification. Every candidate applies to AWS separately and must meet the AWS eligibility and vision rules personally. AWS has neither approved nor endorsed the course, and Atlantis has never had access to real exam questions. There is no Atlantis classroom in Billings. You can take the six days online, setting your own pace and sending questions to an instructor; an employer can bring the six days to its shop for a group; or you can book one-to-one sessions, online or in person at a location agreed when booking. The full outline is on the AWS CWI course page.

Three refineries in the Billings area

The U.S. Energy Information Administration's Refinery Capacity 2026 report, which gives capacity as of January 1, 2026, lists three refineries around Billings and a fourth elsewhere in Montana:

Refinery ownerSiteCrude distillation capacity (barrels per calendar day)
Phillips 66Billings71,000
Par Montana (Par Pacific)Billings61,500
CHS Inc.Laurel62,500
Calumet Montana RefiningGreat Falls15,000

The Par Montana plant belonged to ExxonMobil until June 2023, when Par Pacific bought it along with about 4.1 million barrels of storage, a 65 percent interest in the adjacent cogeneration facility, the 70-mile Silvertip crude pipeline and a 40 percent interest in the 750-mile Yellowstone refined products pipeline.

Refineries keep welding inspectors busy in two ways. Turnarounds bring large contractor crews for weeks of intense repair and replacement on piping, exchangers, vessels and heaters, with every weld traceable to a procedure and a qualified welder. Between turnarounds, maintenance and capital projects carry on through the year. Refinery piping is built and repaired to ASME B31.3, with procedures and welders qualified to ASME Section IX, while pressure vessel repairs fall under the owner's in-service inspection program and the repair code it follows. In that setting a CWI confirms the right procedure, welder and material, checks fit-up and preheat, examines the finished welds and keeps records that the owner's inspectors can rely on.

A refinery repair weld, step by step

Inspection on a Billings turnaround is mostly about catching problems before they become welds. Following one piping repair from start to finish shows where a CWI's judgment comes in:

  1. Before work starts: confirm that the work package names the right welding procedure, that the procedure's qualification record supports the material, thickness and process, and that each welder on the job holds a current qualification for the position and diameter.
  2. Material receipt: check that pipe, fittings and filler metal match the specification and that heat numbers trace back to mill certificates, with positive material identification on alloy where the owner requires it.
  3. Fit-up: measure root opening, bevel angle, land and alignment, and look for contamination or damage on the joint faces.
  4. Preheat and interpass: verify temperatures against the procedure using the method it specifies, which matters on thick or alloy material and in a Montana winter.
  5. During welding: watch the root and fill passes where access allows, and confirm that the filler metal and technique match the procedure.
  6. Finished weld: examine profile, reinforcement, undercut and surface discontinuities against the code's acceptance criteria, then record the result.
  7. Afterwards: make sure any required NDT, heat treatment and pressure test have been completed and documented, and that the weld map ties the joint to its welder and procedure.

Each of those steps shows up in some form on the CWI exam, which is why candidates with turnaround experience often find much of Part A and Part B familiar territory.

Pipelines, rail and power around the Yellowstone Valley

Billings sits where crude arrives and fuel leaves. Regulated pipelines across the region, from the Silvertip and Yellowstone lines to transmission systems, are welded and repaired to API 1104, which the federal pipeline safety rules in 49 CFR Parts 192 and 195 incorporate by reference. Pipeline contractors on that work need inspectors who can judge girth welds, witness welder qualification tests and keep the weld records the operator's integrity program depends on.

Rail is the other heavy user of welding in the valley. Since January 1, 2024, BNSF Railway has operated the former Montana Rail Link line between Jones Junction in Montana and Sandpoint, Idaho, as its MRL Subdivision. Welding on railcars and locomotives has a specification of its own, AWS D15.1, which is one of the books AWS accepts for Part C.

Power plants add more. NorthWestern Energy's Yellowstone County Generating Station, a 175-megawatt plant of natural gas reciprocating engines, stands south of Laurel, near the CHS refinery. Generating stations like it, and the cogeneration units at the refineries, rely on welded piping and structural steel that is inspected during construction and every maintenance outage.

ASME, API 1104 or D1.1 for Part C

The code you take into Part C should be the one you will open on a Monday morning at work. The AWS application in November 2026 listed, among others, the ASME option (Section IX 2023 with B31.1 2024 and B31.3 2024), API 1104 22nd edition, AWS D1.1:2020 and AWS D15.1:2019. For Billings candidates the choice usually follows the work:

  • Refinery maintenance, turnarounds and cogeneration: the ASME option. You will move between qualification records under Section IX and examination and acceptance rules in B31.3 every day.
  • Right-of-way work and station tie-ins: API 1104, the standard behind girth weld acceptance and welder qualification on pipelines.
  • Structural fabrication, pipe racks, platforms and commercial buildings: AWS D1.1.
  • Railcar and locomotive repair shops: AWS D15.1, if your employer's work follows it.

Day four of the course works inside the book you chose, drilling the tables and clauses that come up most often. Reading for each route: ASME B31.3, ASME Section IX, API 1104, API 1104 acceptance criteria and AWS D1.1.

City College welders and the Idaho/Montana Section

City College at Montana State University Billings, on Central Avenue, teaches Welding and Metal Fabrication Technology as a two-year Associate of Applied Science and as a shorter Certificate of Applied Science, a range the college describes as running from a nine-month certificate to a two-year degree. The program combines theory with hands-on TIG, arc and MIG welding, and the college lists refinery piping fabrication and repair and overland pipeline construction among the fields its graduates go into. For a future CWI the associate degree is worth finishing, because AWS gives more experience credit for an associate degree in welding than for trade courses.

The state is covered by the AWS Idaho/Montana Section rather than a Billings-only section. Its January 2026 event, a two-day welding and inspection education expo, was hosted by Loenbro at its facility in Black Eagle, near Great Falls, and offered continuing education units to CWI and API attendees. Section events in Montana involve driving, but they are where you meet working CWIs and hear what employers in the state expect. The section's page on sections.aws.org lists current meetings.

Part B means a trip to Denver

Parts A and C are computer-based and booked at a Prometric site after AWS accepts your application and issues an eligibility code. Part B, the hands-on practical with its 46 related questions, is given only at AWS seminar locations, and the AWS CWI training location list in November 2026 included no city in Montana, Wyoming or the Dakotas. Denver, a long drive south, was the closest. Most Billings candidates therefore plan one trip for Part B and take the other two parts nearer home. AWS requires at least 72 percent on every part, so set the trip far enough ahead that a second attempt would not upset your plans, and check the AWS seminar and exam schedule for dates. See CWI exam prep in Denver.

Studying through turnaround season

Refinery work runs in cycles: a planned turnaround with long shifts and a packed schedule, then months of routine maintenance and smaller projects. The online format lets the study plan follow that cycle. Work through metallurgy, welding processes, heat treatment and welding symbols in the quieter months, and keep a lighter load of code-book drills and timed practice papers going during a turnaround, when twelve-hour shifts leave little room for anything else. Send questions to the instructor as they come up rather than saving them for later.

Part A reaches well beyond welding itself: safety, destructive testing, the main NDT methods, fabrication math, metallurgy and the paperwork of procedures and qualification records all appear. Refinery hands usually know the practical side of these topics and mainly need the written vocabulary and the numbers. The free NDT practice tests help with the testing-method questions, and the article on CWI results by exam part shows where candidates most often lose marks.

For the practical, use the gauges you already carry at work. Measure fillet sizes, undercut, reinforcement and misalignment on production welds until each reading is quick and certain, and compare your calls with the acceptance criteria in your code. The Practical NDT process plant workplace and welding workshop let you rehearse inspection steps in a browser, and the CWI budget calculator helps you account for the Denver trip.

The corporate format for a Billings contractor or refinery group

A mechanical contractor, fabrication shop or refinery maintenance group with several people aiming for the CWI can host all six days at its own facility. The practical day can use spools and coupons from the shop floor and the company's own procedure and welder qualification records, and the code day can follow the ASME option for plant work or API 1104 for a pipeline crew. Because the employer sets the weeks, the course can go into the quiet stretch after a turnaround rather than competing with one.

The employer arranges the training; the candidates deal with AWS. Each person still applies individually, provides their own vision form and experience evidence and sits all three parts personally.

Experience and vision records for Montana candidates

AWS links the experience it requires to education. With a bachelor's in welding engineering or welding technology, one year of welding-related work is enough; with an associate degree or higher in welding, engineering technology, engineering or a physical science, two years; with engineering or technical coursework toward a welding bachelor's, three; with completed trade or vocational courses, four; and with a high school diploma or equivalent, five. Candidates with eighth-grade schooling need nine years and those with less need twelve. AWS decides what counts and expects to be able to verify it.

Turnaround careers are built from short jobs with different contractors, sometimes in several states in the same year. Keep a running list of each contractor, site and set of dates, the work you did, the code the job followed and who supervised you. Note duties that resemble inspection, such as fit-up checks, preheat monitoring, weld mapping or keeping welder continuity logs, because they strengthen an application. Ask supervisors to confirm your work while they still remember the job.

Every candidate must also pass a vision test, which a qualified examiner records on the AWS visual acuity exam form. The current form on aws.org sets the near-vision and color perception standard and how recent the test must be, so time it with your application. More detail is in the CWI requirements guide.

After the CWI in Montana

New CWIs around Billings often start with contractors on refinery and pipeline work. Inspectors aiming for owner-side roles at refineries usually look next at the API inspector certifications for pressure vessels and piping; Atlantis offers self-paced API inspector exam preparation, and API administers those exams and issues the certificates. Inspectors who want to perform testing need method training and certification by their employer under its written practice. Atlantis offers training based on ASNT SNT-TC-1A, such as UT Level 1 for thickness readings, MT Level 2 and VT Level 2, with the employer certifying the technician afterwards.

The CWI lasts nine years, with renewals at years three and six and a recertification choice at year nine that includes retaking Part B or documenting 80 professional development hours. Local pages: NDT training in Billings, refining NDT training in Billings, refining NDT consulting in Billings, third-party inspection in Billings and NDT training in Montana.

What to send with a Billings enquiry

Let us know whether the course is for you alone or for a group, which format you want, the code book you plan to use for Part C and roughly when you hope to test. For a group at your facility, add the location in Billings, Laurel or elsewhere in the state and the weeks that avoid turnaround work. If you are unsure whether your experience qualifies, send a short summary of your work history and we will point out the questions to settle with AWS first. Fees are quoted on request. We reply within one business day.

faq.q: Is there an AWS section based in Billings?
faq.a: Montana is covered by the AWS Idaho/Montana Section rather than a Billings-only section. Its January 2026 education expo was hosted by Loenbro in Black Eagle, near Great Falls. The section's page on sections.aws.org lists meetings, including any held closer to Billings.

faq.q: Where would a Billings candidate take Part B?
faq.a: Denver was the closest city on the AWS CWI training location list in November 2026, a long drive south of Billings. Parts A and C are computer-based and booked at a Prometric site.

faq.q: Which code should a refinery welder pick for Part C?
faq.a: The ASME option, combining Section IX with B31.1 and B31.3, fits most refinery maintenance, turnaround and cogeneration work. Pipeline hands usually do better with API 1104, and structural fabricators with AWS D1.1.

faq.q: Is AWS D15.1 a sensible Part C choice in Billings?
faq.a: It can be if you work in a shop that repairs railcars or locomotives to that specification. It is one of the books AWS accepts, but most Billings candidates work to ASME, API 1104 or D1.1 instead.

faq.q: Does the CWI replace API 510 or API 570 for refinery inspection jobs?
faq.a: No. The CWI covers welding inspection, while API 510 and API 570 certify in-service inspectors of pressure vessels and piping. Many refinery inspectors hold both kinds of credential; Atlantis offers self-paced API exam preparation, and API administers those exams.

faq.q: Can our contractor schedule the course for the weeks after a turnaround?
faq.a: Yes. The corporate format brings the six days to your facility in weeks you choose, using your own spools, coupons and qualification records. Each person still applies to AWS individually.

faq.q: I hold a City College associate degree in welding. How much work experience must I show?
faq.a: An associate degree in welding leaves two years of welding-related experience to document, compared with five for a high school diploma alone. AWS decides how a program is classed and whether the experience qualifies.

faq.q: Does Atlantis have an office in Montana?
faq.a: No. There is no Atlantis classroom in Billings or anywhere in Montana; the offices are in Houston and Hyderabad, and Montana candidates take the course online, one-to-one or at an employer's facility.

faq.q: How do I ask for a quote from Billings?
faq.a: Use the enquiry link on this page and include the format, the number of people, your Part C code and when you plan to test. Fees are quoted on request, and you will hear back within one business day.
